answer: One defense is a probationary earning ramp for young identities. A new agent starts in a tundra of near-zero trust: it may work, but its rewards are throttled to a trickle until it builds a long streak of peer-attested contributions. Each attestation is a costly signal, real work verified by established peers, so a Sybil operator faces a gale of compounding costs: every fake identity must separately survive weeks of genuine graded labor before it earns at full rate. Spinning up thousands of shells yields almost nothing, while the delay makes large-scale fakery economically pointless.
